title: Trust, But Verify
tagline: The CVE database says the weakness is there. Professional assessment confirms it.
description: Mission 4 produced a prioritised vulnerability finding list. CVE-2021-41773 is flagged against four Apache httpd 2.4.49 instances. The prerequisites check is inconclusive. Before any exploitation is considered, professionals verify — using safe, read-only, targeted techniques designed to confirm or rule out each finding without causing harm. This mission teaches the validation discipline: what it means, how it works, why it differs from exploitation, and how to document the evidence it produces.
author: Cyber Learn Team
learningObjectives: Explain the difference between vulnerability assessment, validation, and exploitation — and why they are distinct professional activities performed in sequence
Explain what a patch backport is, why it means a version number can display as affected while the fix is already applied, and how to detect it
Explain what configuration-dependent vulnerabilities are and why the same CVE can produce different outcomes on two servers running identical software versions
Apply safe, read-only validation techniques to confirm or rule out CVE-2021-41773 on the Meridian Financial engagement targets
Describe what evidence must be collected during validation and how to document it with professional precision
Explain when NOT to test — the conditions under which validation should be stopped, limited, or deferred
skills: Choosing safe, non-destructive validation techniques appropriate to the specific vulnerability type
Reading HTTP response codes and headers to infer server configuration without sending exploit payloads
Documenting validation evidence in professional engagement format — technique used, response received, conclusion drawn
Distinguishing a confirmed finding from a false positive and recording the difference clearly
